body:
#2050 (BUG-1555 CRLF PROBE) APPROVED at 3402cbdaac76, with a disclosure and
two findings worth fixing before the probe is relied on.

DISCLOSURE: I SPECIFIED THIS MEASUREMENT. I recommended the probe, ruled out
the log shortcut, and said what it should emit. I did not author the change
and did not merge it, so reviewing is in role - but you should decide whether
a reviewer who wrote the spec for a diagnostic is the right independent party
for it. I would not object to a second look. Flagging rather than deciding.

WHAT IS RIGHT ABOUT IT, including something they did not claim: the step runs
on BOTH matrix legs, so macOS is a built-in control. Windows CRLF against
macOS LF is the discriminating observation rather than a bare Windows reading.
That is better than what I asked for.

VERIFIED RATHER THAN ACCEPTED, per the standard:
  wiring   step at cross-platform.yml:80 in the build job; checkout at :54,
           so the files exist when it runs. Right job, right order.
  fires    I ran probe_file locally against known-CRLF, known-LF and a
           missing path: CRLF / LF / ABSENT, three distinct outputs. Their
           demonstration claim holds and is now independently reproduced.

TWO ENUMERATION DEFECTS. Neither blocks the observation - core.autocrlf is
printed directly and is decisive alone - but both are the shape this spec
exists to catalogue.

1. THE HEADLINE PAIR USES THE ONE EXEMPT FILE. It labels README.md as "the
   two sides the drift test compares". README.md is a
   LOCALIZED_DISCIPLINE_GUIDES entry - one of the 3 EXCLUDED, not one of the
   23 compared. The printed values are still informative (identical checkout
   treatment), so the conclusion would be right and the LABEL is what is
   false. On a spec about an instrument that misreports, a diagnostic
   mislabelling its own subject should not ship that way.

2. THE ONE THAT MATTERS LATER: the loop is `.aida/discipline/*.md` and misses
   glossary.yaml - 26 of 27 - which IS in the compared set and DID fail on the
   09-21 nightly, while the step claims "every tracked project-copy guide".
   Low impact today. REAL IF THE FIX IS WRITTEN NARROWLY: a .gitattributes
   rule written as *.md rather than covering .aida/discipline/** would leave
   the yaml unpinned, and this probe - the instrument meant to CONFIRM the fix
   - would report all-LF and never show it. Blind in exactly the dimension it
   will be trusted for. Glob the directory, not the extension.

Also recorded: probe_file reports CRLF on ANY carriage return, so it detects
"contains CR" not "uses CRLF line endings" (a lone mid-line CR reads CRLF -
verified). Right bias for a diagnostic; noted so the output is not over-read.

Merge-readiness recorded separately: BLOCKED at this sha, code verdict only.

#1981 Build still in_progress. Re-verify armed.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #2050 approved w/ disclosure (I specified this probe) - 2 enumeration findings, #2 blinds the probe to the narrow-gitattributes fix
